verification_report.summary:
The complete proof passes the sequential audit under the explicitly supplied internal premises. No finiteness of either original Monge–Ampere measure, no bounded mass property, and no identification of the convex-competitor class with a volume-equality class is used.

The preliminary envelope constructions preserve the exact all-b competitor condition. Semipositivity justifies the rescalings and bounded truncations. In the zero-domination lemma, q=P_{delta theta}(v) is genuine because delta>epsilon. Stretching w by 1/beta and scaling every defining competitor proves beta z belongs to E_env(X,beta theta,0). It supplies a lower competitor for k=P_{beta theta}(u-q); the positive-volume/L1 envelope bound gives sup k<infinity. The difference obstacle is quasi-continuous and finite almost everywhere off the ignored pluripolar sets. The stipulated general-contact theorem applies without a mass bound, and canonical representatives give k+q<=u everywhere. Upward stability therefore places k in the required class.

Contact and positive mixed products give nu_k<=1_{k+q=u}mu_u. On contact where k<0, one has u<q<=v, so nu_k({k<0})=0. Since {k>=0} is contained in {k>-1}, plurifine locality identifies nu_k there with the measure of the single bounded potential max(k,-1). This proves nu_k(X)<infinity before finite-measure domination is invoked. Reference zero satisfies all reference hypotheses in beta theta, and the bounded-potential scaling bijection gives v_-(beta theta)=beta^n v_-(theta)>0. Thus the finite theorem applies legitimately to k and zero and yields u>=q. The displayed interpolation with a fixed smaller-background envelope then tends to v almost everywhere; canonical representatives give u=v everywhere.

In both domination arguments, subtraction is performed on common sets where every relevant potential exceeds a finite truncation level. Each restricted measure is finite, so the strictly positive coefficient difference forces the required vanishing; exhaustion discards only pluripolar sets. The earlier finite theorem obtains its coefficient-one bound by ordered contact and uses finiteness only for the fixed-measure tail that prevents collapse. The new strict theorem instead applies the proved zero lemma to p<=u after establishing mu_p({p<u})=0. The exponential and constant-shift corollaries remain valid for extended measures off their pole sets.

The dependency chain is acyclic: preliminary envelope/contact results, finite-measure domination, auxiliary finiteness, zero domination, strict domination, then the corollaries. Neither the proposed conclusion nor prescribed-reference existence is used as a premise. The cited definitions and finite-case scope agree with [ALS26](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02339v1) and [XL26](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13446v1); XL26's bounded-mass results are not applied outside that setting.
